text:
maya: Heads up — CI perf alert for PR #5238 (merged ~2h ago). perf-bot shows kv_batched_infer microbench p95 +18% vs baseline :warning:
perf-bot: [auto] benchmark kv_batched_infer: baseline=12.4ms p95, current=14.6ms p95, delta=+17.7% (threshold 5%) — failing
liam: ugh. which commit/merge caused this?
sahil: CI link? logs?
perf-bot: https://ci.internal.redwood/bench/5238/output — summary + full perf diff attached (see artifacts).
jun: quick skim: there was a late merge that changed kernel selection policy for short sequences (commit 9f3a21d). ping @liam since he owned the PR that touched batcher heuristics.
liam: that's me. the PR was supposed to improve tail-latency for big batches. didn't touch kv cache. 9f3a21d modifies `KernelSelector::choose` fallback path.
maya: can someone run `git bisect` locally against the perf benchmark? we need a bisect result before the release freeze meeting in 30m.
sahil: starting a bisect job on my workstation now. will report.
ci-bot: CI job queued: bisect-perf-run (kv_batched_infer) — assigned to sahil — est 18m
sahil: first pass: seems to point at 9f3a21d -> revert of that commit locally makes microbench p95 go back to 12.5ms.
liam: hmm, that commit trades off short-sequence kernel choice to prefer smaller-memory kernels for cache locality. Maybe eviction patterns changed.
jun: can you paste the microbench trace? any spike in memcpy or kernel launch time?
sahil: paste:
```
# perf trace (shortened)
call: forward_batch 0 -> 1.8ms
launch kernel_small (SGEMM)  -> 0.9ms
launch kernel_large (ATTN)  -> 3.2ms
KV cache lookup hit rate: 98.7% -> after merge 91.1%
KV cache evictions/sec: 2.1 -> 9.7
```
liam: whoa KV hit rate drop is suspicious — my change shouldn't touch cache indexing but could change memory footprint -> eviction increase.
maya: data point: this only shows up under the microbench synthetic workload with lots of short prefixes (seq len 8-12) and a wide range of batch sizes — production traces haven't shown issues yet, but we can't risk release.
perf-bot: additional artifact: heap_snapshot_176900_1.json (link). shows per-worker cache usage higher by ~22% on the failing run.
jun: proposed immediate action: revert 9f3a21d from main, run CI perf job, then reapply with instrumentation. agreed?
liam: I can open an emergency revert PR and request fast-track. prepping now.
release-bot: Release policy: emergency revert allowed during freeze window with +2 approvers from eng-runtime.
maya: @sahil can you run the CI perf job against the revert branch once it's up?
sahil: yes — will trigger and report numbers.
liam: opened PR #5242 revert kernel-selection fallback (link). cc @jun for review.
ci-bot: running microbench suite on pr/5242...
perf-bot: result: kv_batched_infer p95=12.6ms baseline 12.4ms delta +1.6% (within threshold) — PASS
maya: ok that's promising. revert PR looks safe.
liam: will merge revert after +2 approvals. @jun @sahil can you review quickly?
jun: approving now. also creating a follow-up PR to add KV cache diagnostic counters and a perf test that simulates short-prefix workloads.
sahil: merged revert PR. CI afterwards shows perf stable.
liam: further action items: (1) add perf unit that reproduces eviction regression (2) add memory-usage guard in kernel selector to avoid increasing working set (3) postmortem notes. I'll own 1+2.
maya: thanks all — excellent quick work. filing a rollout blocker ticket and marking release unblocked after revert: https://issues.redwood/ENG-8739
liam: reminder — when we reintroduce the change, let's run the new perf test matrix and run kv-batch heavy production canary.
perf-bot: note: tagging thread with label perf-regression, rollback — automated summary sent to #incidents. :white_check_mark:
